features.name: Landing_Page
features.purpose: Introduces BWS4 to visitors, explains that it and every example app were built using Spec4, and provides a way to discover and open each available example app.

invocation.trigger: A user navigates to the application's main entry point.

inputs.name: example app listing
inputs.description: The set of currently available example apps, each with a name and short description.

outputs.primary: An introductory view naming BWS4, explaining its Spec4 provenance, and listing each example app with a short description and a way to open it.
outputs.schema_notes: Each listed entry includes an app name, a one- or two-line description, and an entry point into that app.

success_criteria: Every currently available example app appears in the listing and can be opened from it.
The explanatory text clearly states that BWS4 and all its example apps were built using Spec4.
Newly added example apps appear in the listing without requiring changes elsewhere.

failure_modes.mode: A new example app is added but does not appear on the landing page.
failure_modes.mitigation: The listing is guaranteed to reflect the current set of available apps rather than a fixed snapshot.

failure_modes.mode: An entry links to an app that fails to open.
failure_modes.mitigation: Each entry's link is confirmed valid before being shown.

features.name: RAG_Example_App
features.purpose: Illustrates the Retrieval-Augmented Generation pattern by answering user questions using a small, public dataset as a grounding source, for educational rather than task-specific purposes.

invocation.trigger: A user opens the app and submits a question.

inputs.name: user question
inputs.description: A free-form question the user wants answered using the dataset.

inputs.name: reference dataset
inputs.description: A small, publicly available, pre-loaded set of documents used as the retrieval source for answers.

outputs.primary: An answer to the user's question, accompanied by the specific passages that supported it.
outputs.schema_notes: Includes the generated answer plus a list of the retrieved passages used to produce it.

success_criteria: Answers are grounded in and traceable to passages actually retrieved from the dataset.
Retrieved passages shown alongside the answer are relevant to the question.
A short explanation of the retrieval-then-generate pattern is presented to the user.
The app behaves reasonably across a range of sample questions about the dataset's subject matter.

failure_modes.mode: Retrieval surfaces passages unrelated to the question.
failure_modes.mitigation: Retrieved passages are relevance-checked before being used to generate the answer.

failure_modes.mode: The generated answer disregards the retrieved passages.
failure_modes.mitigation: Retrieved passages are shown alongside the answer so any mismatch is visible to the user.

failure_modes.mode: The reference dataset is unavailable when the app runs.
failure_modes.mitigation: The dataset is bundled with the app so it is always available.

features.name: Shared_Framework_Services
features.purpose: Provides the common text-generation, embedding, web-search, and small-scale data-persistence capabilities that every example app relies on, so each app can be built without recreating these capabilities itself.

invocation.trigger: Any example app requests text generation, an embedding, a search, or persistence of a small piece of data.

inputs.name: request type
inputs.description: Which capability is being requested: generation, embedding, search, or persistence.

inputs.name: request payload
inputs.description: The prompt, text to embed, search query, or data record relevant to the request.

outputs.primary: A capability-specific result: generated text, a numeric representation of meaning for given text, a set of search results, or confirmation that data was stored or retrieved.
outputs.schema_notes: Each response is tagged with the request type and the requesting app so results can be matched to their originating request.

success_criteria: Any example app can obtain a generation, embedding, search, or persistence result without implementing that capability itself.
The same embedding capability produces consistent, comparable results across all apps that use it.
Data submitted for persistence can reliably be retrieved again later.
An unavailable or malfunctioning underlying capability is detectable rather than silently producing a wrong result.

failure_modes.mode: An underlying capability is temporarily unavailable.
failure_modes.mitigation: Requests fail with a clear, retriable signal rather than returning a silently incorrect result.

failure_modes.mode: Different apps end up using inconsistent embedding behavior.
failure_modes.mitigation: A single shared embedding capability is used by all apps that need embeddings.

failure_modes.mode: Persisted data is lost or not retrievable later.
failure_modes.mitigation: The persistence guarantee is verified before apps depend on it.

features.name: Tool_Use_Integration
features.purpose: Gives example apps the ability to perform a live web search step as part of demonstrating tool-use and agentic patterns, so a model's request for external information can be fulfilled and fed back into its process.

invocation.trigger: An example app's process determines it needs current external information and issues a search request as a tool step.

inputs.name: search query
inputs.description: The query the requesting app needs answered via external search.

inputs.name: result count
inputs.description: How many search results to return.

outputs.primary: A list of relevant search results that the requesting app can present or feed into a further step.
outputs.schema_notes: Each result includes a title, a short snippet, and a reference to its source.

success_criteria: Search requests return results relevant to the query.
Results are usable as input to the requesting app's next step without further reformatting.
A failed or unavailable search is surfaced to the user rather than silently ignored.

failure_modes.mode: The external search capability is temporarily unavailable.
failure_modes.mitigation: The requesting app is informed the tool step failed and degrades gracefully instead of stalling.

failure_modes.mode: Returned results are irrelevant to the query.
failure_modes.mitigation: The query is passed through unmodified and relevance is visible to the user for evaluation.

failure_modes.mode: Search usage limits are reached during heavy use.
failure_modes.mitigation: Search usage is capped so the app remains responsive rather than failing unpredictably.

features.name: Embeddings_Example_App
features.purpose: Demonstrates the embedding pattern through a visual explorer that plots pre-configured text examples in a shared 2D space to show semantic clustering, and lets users add their own text to see where it lands.

invocation.trigger: A user opens the app, or submits custom text for inclusion in the visualization.

inputs.name: preset text set
inputs.description: A curated built-in set of word/short-phrase categories and full sentences used to populate the initial visualization.

inputs.name: custom text
inputs.description: Text a user enters to be embedded and merged into the visualization.

outputs.primary: A two-dimensional visualization of all text points, grouped by semantic similarity, with any custom user text shown in a visually distinct color.
outputs.schema_notes: Each point carries its source text, its category (if preset), and its position; custom points are flagged separately from preset points.

success_criteria: Semantically related preset texts appear visually close together, and unrelated ones appear farther apart.
Submitted custom text is embedded, merged into the same visualization, and rendered in a distinct color from preset points.
A short explanation of what embeddings are and what the visualization shows is presented to the user.
The visualization uses the same shared embedding capability used elsewhere in the framework, so results are consistent.

failure_modes.mode: The 2D projection distorts true semantic similarity.
failure_modes.mitigation: The projection is chosen to preserve relative closeness as well as reasonably possible and is described to the user as an approximation.
A clear error is shown and the prior visualization remains unaffected.

failure_modes.mode: The plot becomes cluttered and hard to read with many points.
failure_modes.mitigation: Point labels and details are available on demand rather than all shown at once.

features.name: Single_Call_Example_App
features.purpose: Demonstrates the single-call pattern: one direct request to a model producing one direct response, with no retrieval, tools, or multi-step chaining, in both plain and structured response modes.

invocation.trigger: A user enters or selects a prompt, chooses a response mode, and submits.

inputs.name: prompt text
inputs.description: A free-form prompt entered by the user.

inputs.name: preset prompt selection
inputs.description: A choice from a set of example prompts such as summarize, classify, or extract.

inputs.name: mode selection
inputs.description: Whether the request should use Simple mode (plain text) or Structured mode (schema-conforming response).

outputs.primary: A single model response corresponding to the submitted prompt and selected mode.
outputs.format: plain text, or structured data shown alongside the request that produced it
outputs.schema_notes: In Structured mode, the output includes both the structured request submitted and the structured response returned, displayed together.

success_criteria: Simple mode returns a readable plain-text response to the submitted prompt.
Structured mode returns a response that conforms to the requested structure and shows both the request and response to the user.
A short explanation of the single-call pattern and when it is appropriate is presented.
No retrieval, tool use, or multi-step chaining occurs as part of producing the response.

failure_modes.mode: The structured response does not conform to the requested structure.
failure_modes.mitigation: Nonconformance is detected and shown to the user rather than presented as if it succeeded.

failure_modes.mode: Users are unsure what a preset prompt will do.
failure_modes.mitigation: Preset prompts are labeled with their intent, such as summarize, classify, or extract.

failure_modes.mode: A user submits with no prompt and no preset chosen.
failure_modes.mitigation: Submission is blocked until a valid prompt or preset is provided.

nfr_goals: Each example app responds to user actions within a few seconds under normal conditions.
The collection of example apps can grow over time without disrupting apps that are already in use.
All example apps share a consistent navigation and layout experience.
The framework can run using freely accessible generation, embedding, and search capabilities, without requiring paid access for basic evaluation.
The application is fully usable directly in a web browser without additional installation.
